transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, I suppose what brings me in is… I just can’t seem to sit still much anymore. For the past year or so, I’m always puttering around—fixing this, arranging that, signing up to help with one more thing. Even at my age, 87, you’d think I’d be content to sit with a cup of tea, but no, I’m up again straightening something or finding a little task to do.
Do you have times when your energy becomes much higher than is usual for you?

Yes, I suppose so—though I don’t know if I’d call it “higher” exactly. It’s more that I’m just always up and doing something lately. For the past year or so, I’ll sit down and then notice a drawer needs sorting, or I’ll go fix something, or I’ll volunteer for one more little thing at church—well, not always church, sometimes it’s the neighbor’s garden club, you know how those things go. Even at 87, I have such a hard time just staying put and being still.
Have you been needing less sleep than usual?

I’m not really sure I’d say that. My sleep is… well, it varies, you know, especially at my age. Some nights I’m up to use the bathroom or I hear a noise and then I think about whether I locked the back door—my late husband was always particular about that. But needing less sleep? I haven’t really noticed that, no.
During these times when you’re always up and doing things, do you feel unusually cheerful or high in spirit?

Unusually cheerful? Hmm… I don’t know that I’d say that, exactly. I mean, I like to keep busy, and sometimes it feels good to get things done—my mother was always that way too, always polishing something or moving a vase from one table to another—but I don’t think I feel especially high-spirited or anything. Just… occupied, I suppose.
Have you been having trouble with your memory lately?

Memory? Well… I suppose everyone my age misplaces a pair of glasses now and then, don’t they? I’ll walk into the kitchen and then think, “Now what did I come in here for?”—but then I’ll see the kettle and remember I was making tea. My sister used to say she could never find her keys, and she was younger than me. So… I don’t know that I’d call it trouble, exactly. What sort of memory trouble do you mean?
Have your memory problems made it hard for you to manage your day-to-day tasks on your own?

Hard to manage things? I don’t… I don’t think so. I still do my usual bits around the house, though sometimes I get distracted halfway through—like I’ll start sorting the mail and then notice a plant needs water, and then I remember my neighbor used to keep the most beautiful geraniums. But as far as not being able to manage on my own, no, I haven’t really noticed that.
Have other people told you that you’ve been talking more than usual?

Talking more than usual? I’m not sure anyone’s said that to me directly. I do like to chat, I suppose—especially if someone brings up the neighborhood or family, because then one thing reminds me of another. My late cousin could talk for hours, really, she’d start with the weather and end up telling you about a recipe from 1946. But no… I don’t think people have told me I’m talking more than usual.
Has anyone close to you told you they are worried about your memory?

Worried about my memory? Not that I can think of, no. My daughter might remind me about appointments, but she reminds everyone—she’s always been the organized one, even as a girl, had her school pencils all lined up just so. But no, I don’t think anyone’s sat me down and said they’re worried about my memory.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot?

Worrying a lot… well, I don’t know if I’d call it a lot. I suppose everyone worries a little, don’t they? Bills and whether the oven’s off, and oh, my mother used to go back to check the stove three times before we’d leave for church. But me, I haven’t really noticed myself worrying more than usual, no.
When you’re up and doing things, do you feel nervous or on edge?

Nervous or on edge when I’m up doing things… hmm. I can’t say I’ve really noticed that. I do like to keep busy, you know, puttering around, straightening a drawer or looking for something I meant to do—and then sometimes I end up finding old birthday cards instead, which can take you right down memory lane. But nervous? I don’t think that’s quite it.
Have you gotten lost in places that should be familiar to you?

Gotten lost… no, I don’t think so. I mean, I still know my way around the neighborhood and the grocery store I go to—though they keep moving the bread aisle, which drives me mad. But lost in a familiar place, no, not that I can recall.
Do you often go back to check things, like whether the door is locked or the stove is off?

Oh, checking the door or the stove… I don’t think I do that especially, no. I mean, sometimes if I’m leaving I’ll jiggle the doorknob because that’s just what you do, isn’t it? My father always did that, gave it a good tug like he was trying to pull the whole house down. But going back over and over to check, I haven’t really noticed myself doing that.
Have you had trouble recognizing people you know well?

Recognizing people I know well… I don’t think I’ve had trouble with that, no. If it’s someone I know, like family or an old friend, I know them. Now names, sometimes they come a little slower—well, that happens to everyone at my age, doesn’t it? I ran into a woman at church once and we talked about the bake sale, and I was thinking more about whether I’d left the muffins in too long than anything else. But recognizing people close to me, no, I haven’t noticed a problem.
Do you have trouble relaxing?

Yes, relaxing is… well, that’s part of why I came in, I suppose. I don’t seem to sit still very well anymore—or maybe I never did, but this past year or so it’s been more noticeable. I’m always puttering around, straightening this, fixing that, rearranging a drawer that was perfectly fine.

I’ll sit down with a cup of tea and then I notice the magazines are crooked, or I remember someone at church needs help with something, and up I go. Even at 87, you’d think I’d have earned the right to just sit, but I’m always taking on one more little thing. It’s hard for me to just be still.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different things?

Worrying about many different things… I’m not sure. I mean, everyone worries some, don’t they? Bills, family, whether the weather’s going to turn before you get the laundry in—though I don’t hang it out much anymore, not like my mother did with those wooden clothespins.

But I don’t know that I’d say I spend a lot of time worrying. I suppose things cross my mind, but I can’t really tell if it’s more than normal.
Do you get tired easily?

Tired easily… hmm. I don’t know that I’ve really noticed. Some days I feel a bit worn out, but then again, at 87, who wouldn’t after doing errands or fussing around the house? Yesterday I went to look for a button in my sewing tin and ended up sorting the whole thing by color, which wasn’t what I meant to do at all.

But tired easily, specifically… I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say it’s something I’ve been keeping track of.
Have you been feeling more irritable than usual?

More irritable… I’m not sure, honestly. I do get a bit short sometimes if something isn’t where I left it, or if the phone rings right when I’ve finally sat down—but I don’t know if that’s more than usual.

My sister used to say I was “quick to fuss,” even when we were girls, though she was the one who borrowed my hair ribbons and never put them back. So… I suppose I haven’t really noticed a big change.
When you try to sit quietly, do worries start running through your mind?

When I try to sit quietly… well, I’m not sure I sit quietly very often, to tell you the truth. I’ll sit down and then notice a magazine needs straightening, or there’s a little thread on my sleeve, or I remember the kettle—though I don’t always remember why I got up.

But worries running through my mind? I don’t know. I suppose thoughts come and go, but I haven’t really noticed them being worries exactly. It’s more just… my mind wandering, I think.
Do you often feel physically tense, like your muscles are tight?

Physically tense… like tight muscles? I don’t know that I’d say that. I mean, sometimes my shoulders feel up around my ears if I’ve been concentrating on something, like trying to thread a needle—though the light in my sitting room isn’t what it used to be, I’ve been meaning to change that bulb.

But as a usual thing, feeling tight all over… I haven’t really paid attention to that. I’m not sure.
When worries do come up, do you find it hard to stop or control them?

I’m not sure I’d put it that way… hard to stop them. I don’t think of them as worries so much as thoughts that wander in and out.

Sometimes I’ll be thinking about one thing and then suddenly I’m remembering I meant to call someone, or that I left a note on the kitchen table—oh, and my kitchen table has all these little scraps of paper, which I keep meaning to sort, because half of them are probably old grocery lists. But as for controlling worries… I don’t really know. I haven’t noticed that being a big problem.
